history.ask: What the beat feels like (ask patient to tap it out)
options: Gradual pounding that builds and settles
Stops with breath-holding / straining / cold water
Coffee, tea, energy drinks, or smoking
Heavy menstrual bleeding or black stools
Known ischaemic or structural heart disease
Family history of sudden death < 40 years

red_flags: Associated chest pain or severe dyspnoea
Family history of sudden cardiac death under 40
Known structural heart disease or prior myocardial infarction with new sustained palpitations
Heart rate > 150/min with hypotension at presentation
exam: Palpate the radial pulse for a full minute — rate and whether irregularly irregular
Confirm apex–radial deficit by auscultating the apex while palpating the pulse (atrial fibrillation)
Measure BP and repeat after 3 minutes standing if episodes occur on standing
Auscultate the heart for murmurs — mitral disease predisposes to AF; ejection murmur raises structural disease
Look for thyroid signs: fine tremor of outstretched hands, sweaty palms, lid lag
Palpate the neck for goitre and listen for a thyroid bruit
Inspect conjunctivae and palmar creases for pallor
Auscultate lung bases for crackles — rapid AF with pulmonary congestion changes urgency
Estimate JVP and look for pedal oedema (heart failure from sustained arrhythmia)
Observe breathing pattern and reproduce symptoms with voluntary hyperventilation if panic is suspected

investigations.why: Captures the rhythm if symptoms are ongoing — rules AF or SVT in on the spot; between episodes it screens for pre-excitation (WPW), long QT, and old infarction that mark a dangerous substrate

investigations.test: TSH (add free T4 if TSH suppressed)
investigations.why: Directly rules thyrotoxicosis in or out — a suppressed TSH explains sinus tachycardia and new AF; normal TSH removes it from the list
Low haemoglobin rules in anaemia as the driver of compensatory sinus tachycardia; normal CBC pushes toward primary arrhythmia or panic

investigations.test: Electrolytes and renal function (K, Mg where available, Ca)
investigations.why: Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia provoke ectopy and sustained arrhythmia — correctable findings that explain the symptom
Hypoglycaemic episodes present with tremor and pounding heart — a low value during symptoms rules this in, especially in diabetics on treatment

investigations.test: Ambulatory ECG (Holter 24–48 h) or event recording
investigations.why: When the resting ECG is normal and episodes are recurrent — correlates the felt symptom with the actual rhythm, separating ectopics and paroxysmal AF/SVT from sinus rhythm during panic
If murmur, abnormal ECG, or documented sustained arrhythmia — rules structural disease (mitral valve disease, cardiomyopathy) in or out, which decides how seriously ectopy is taken

supports: Fast, completely irregular beat felt by the patient
Irregularly irregular pulse with apex–radial deficit
Mitral murmur, thyrotoxicosis signs, or alcohol history
Irregular rhythm without P waves on ECG
Abrupt-onset, abrupt-offset regular racing lasting minutes to hours
Terminates with vagal manoeuvres (straining, cold water)
Pre-excitation (short PR, delta wave) on resting ECG
Isolated skipped or extra thumps, seconds long, at rest
Worse with coffee, smoking, or stress
Ectopics captured on ECG or Holter with structurally normal heart
Sustained regular palpitations with syncope, exertional onset, or chest pain
Known ischaemic or structural heart disease
Family history of sudden death under 40
Weight loss with good appetite, heat intolerance, tremor
Goitre, lid lag, or thyroid bruit on exam
Suppressed TSH with raised free T4
Gradual pounding with fatigue and exertional dyspnoea
Pallor of conjunctivae and palmar creases
Menorrhagia or black stools
Low haemoglobin on CBC
Episodes with fear, choking sensation, and tingling, triggered by stress
Gradual build and fade, at rest, never with syncope
Normal ECG during a captured symptomatic episode
Clear temporal link to caffeine, decongestants, inhaler overuse, or supplements
Regular gradual-onset tachycardia that settles with abstinence
Normal TSH, CBC, and resting ECG
